key_insight: A simulator-trained inverse map lets Bayesian optimization search a low-dimensional space while preserving the original problem geometry through its Gaussian process kernel.
engineering_relevance: Engineers can leverage mechanistic simulators to reduce online black-box search complexity rather than optimizing directly over all control variables.
method: Train an amortized inverse map offline to predict optimal controls from simulator parameters.
Run Bayesian optimization over the learned representation using a geometry-aware Gaussian process kernel.
Analyze approximation bias, information gain, and regret dependence on intrinsic dimension under additional assumptions.
evidence_signal: Numerical simulations of personalized Parkinson’s drug dosing report improved optimization performance, including under simulator misspecification.
watch_item: Restricting search to the learned representation can introduce approximation bias; the regret result requires additional geometric and Gaussian process assumptions.
paper_title: Bayesian optimization on amortized search space
